newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end higher as yen weakens.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end higher as yen weakens.

text.p: Yen-based precious metal futures ended higher in Tokyo on Monday, with the yen's renewed fall against the dollar offsetting a dip in bullion prices.
"It has not risen enough considering the yen's sharp fall," said one trader, adding that profit-taking by speculators limited topside.

TOCOM benchmark February 1998 gold gained 10 yen, while other months were nine to 17 yen better. Bullion was quoted at $347.65/8.15 an ounce, down marginally from Friday's New York closing quote of $348.50/349.00. In early Tokyo afternoon, the dollar hit 125.00 yen, its highest in 50 months, before easing.

Foreign exchange dealers said a possible rise in U.S. interest rates and a feeling in the market that the U.S. still wanted to see a strong dollar helped the dollar rise despite stronger-that expected Japanese trade data.

Yen-based white metals also finished higher, helped by remarks by a Russian official that there would be no Russian shipments of platinum group metals to Japan in April and that May shipments were also in doubt. He also said Russian platinum group metal exports for 1997 would be much lower than in 1996.
Another trader said: "White metals will be supported at the levels as uncertainties over Russian shipments remain."
